findings.finding: launch_manager's generic exception handler logs, sets pipeline_state='blocked' and sends an alert, but never calls transition_task. A failure after the coding transition (L500) leaves the task stuck in 'coding'; a failure before it (e.g. worktree creation L496) leaves it in 'ready_for_review'. restart_task refuses planning/coding/testing (409) and run_task accepts only pending/rejected/blocked, so no API/UI recovery exists without a manual PATCH.
findings.evidence: agents.py:615-620 (no transition); the identical bug class was explicitly fixed for launch_planning_pipeline (agents.py:257-277, comment 'Blocker (audit_v1.md 4.3 #2) ... never transition the task out of planning ... leaving no self-service recovery path') and launch_coder does transition to blocked (agents.py:1043-1048). Guard evidence: tasks.py:471-481 (_ACTIVE_STATUSES 409), tasks.py:345-348 (run_task statuses), tasks.py:231-244 (manual PATCH escape hatch). Same gap applies to a process crash mid-launch_manager: orphan recovery covers agent_runs rows only (failure_ladder.py:282-422).
findings.production_impact: Any generic exception in the manager pipeline (DB error, artifact write failure, diff capture) orphans the task in an active status with pipeline_state='blocked' but no matching task status; operators must know the undocumented PATCH workaround or the task is unrecoverable except via cancel.
findings.confidence: High (code path unambiguous; recovery paths enumerated)
findings.recommendation: Mirror the planning fix: inside the handler use a fresh session to update_pipeline_state + transition_task(db2, task_id, 'blocked'), swallowing TransitionError/ValueError.

findings.line: 1625-1644 (16 names), 1665-1792 (20 registrations), 1341-1343 (pool_size=16, max_overflow=0), 1375-1398 (connection held for loop lifetime)
findings.finding: The leader-election engine is sized from a 16-entry name tuple, but 20 loops are actually launched with _run_as_leader. Four registered loops are absent from the tuple: loop:versioned_lesson_consolidation (L1685), loop:memory_embeddings_consolidation (L1692), loop:agent_historical_performance_rollup (L1699), loop:documentation_score_compute (L1772). Each winning loop holds its engine connection for its entire lifetime (await run_loop() inside async with engine.connect()), and max_overflow=0, so exactly 4 of 20 tasks block on checkout, hit the default 30s pool timeout, and raise TimeoutError outside any try - permanently dead, no retry.
findings.evidence: main.py:1625-1642 vs 1665-1792 (count mismatch, names verified by diff); main.py:1341-1343 (pool_size=len(_leader_loop_names)=16, max_overflow=0); main.py:1374-1398 (connection held during run_loop; only non-acquirers release and sleep); leader_election_enabled defaults True (config.py:1642-1654) and the comment at main.py:1619-1620 states single-instance 'always wins its own uncontested locks' - so the starvation happens on every default deployment, not just multi-instance. Stale docstring 'One shared engine for all 9' at main.py:1621.
findings.production_impact: On every default deployment at least 4 singleton background loops silently never run (candidates in creation order: prompts_score_compute, documentation_score_compute, enhancement_quality_monitor, dependency_auto_dispatch; whichever 4 lose the checkout race), plus recurring unretrieved TimeoutError tasks. No health check or metric surfaces the dead loops. Carried from AUDIT_03 cross_audit_flags - now scored here.
findings.confidence: High (count mismatch verified; pool mechanics verified; which 4 lose depends on scheduling)
findings.recommendation: Build one tuple of (lock_name, loop) pairs and size the engine from its length (single source of truth); or set max_overflow >= 4 as a stopgap; fix the stale '9' docstring.

findings.location: _planning_node (epic path) - run_planning_pipeline pause never resumed; child DevTask never transitioned; subtasks never persisted
findings.line: 2130-2222 (node), 2168-2180 (DevTask created status='planning'), 2184-2197 (paused result consumed); graph.py:220+174 (pause mechanisms), graph.py:237-240 (docstring 'Stops at human_review checkpoint'); save_subtasks single caller agents.py:190
findings.finding: The epic path calls run_planning_pipeline, which deliberately stops at the human_review checkpoint, but nothing ever resumes or approves that graph for epic-created tasks: no arequest_human_input, no resume_pipeline call, no pipeline_state write. The paused subtasks are consumed pre-approval and _coding_node proceeds. The epic-created DevTask (status='planning') is never transitioned by any epic code path, no Subtask rows are persisted (save_subtasks is only called by launch_planning_pipeline), so run_manager's _db_subtask_rows stays empty and every update_subtask_status is skipped; no diff/files_touched is ever written for epic children.
findings.evidence: manager.py:2184-2197 (subtasks taken from paused graph; no approval recording); grep of manager.py: 13 DevTask/transition matches, none transitions the child task; agents.py:190 (only save_subtasks caller); manager.py:1559-1579 (_db_subtask_rows fetch), 988-1000 (skip guard); epics.py:193-198 (child never appears in batch review since status is 'planning'); tasks.py:471-481 (restart 409), tasks.py:345-348 (run 400).
findings.production_impact: Epic children are permanent ghost rows in 'planning' with no subtask/diff history; the plan-review gate is silently bypassed relative to the task path; one dangling checkpoint thread per epic; the task list and dashboards carry stuck entries no API can move.
findings.confidence: High on mechanics; Medium on whether the bypass is intended (if epic batch review is the intended single gate, the code should still close out the child task and persist subtasks)
findings.recommendation: Decide the epic plan-gate explicitly: either resume the paused graph through a recorded plan_review approval before _coding_node, or invoke planning without the human_review interruption; in both cases call save_subtasks and drive the child DevTask to ready_for_review/blocked at epic terminal.

findings.location: approve_epic / reject_epic - status flip only, no downstream lifecycle actions
findings.finding: Epic approve/reject only set Epic.status and publish an event. Nothing pushes the branch or creates a PR, nothing transitions the child DevTask, nothing records a git-push approval, nothing removes or preserves worktrees. _record_git_push_approval has no epic-path caller; push_and_create_pr's only caller is the task approvals path.
findings.evidence: epics.py:267-278 and 301-312; grep: _record_git_push_approval callers = agents.py:596, 1033 only; push_and_create_pr callers = approvals.py:180 only; task-path close-out does transition 'completed' + remove_worktree (approvals.py:201-224); worktree retention prunes only completed/failed/cancelled tasks (config.py:840-843) which an epic child (ORCH-04-103) never reaches.
findings.production_impact: Approved epics produce no PR and no completion trail; epic worktrees accumulate indefinitely; there is no epic analogue of the task 'completed' terminal state, so epic outcomes cannot feed the same review/push workflow tasks get.
findings.confidence: High (absence of callers verified by grep)
findings.recommendation: Define and implement the epic close-out: on approve, drive child tasks to terminal state and run the worktree/PR decision (or explicitly document that epics deliberately stop at the branch level); on reject, remove epic worktrees.

findings.location: run_manager fan-out wave - shared AsyncSession across concurrent subtasks; publish_event ordering claim
findings.line: 2346 (epic passes enable_fanout=settings.enable_subtask_fanout), config.py:310-314 (default True), manager.py:1643-1664 (gather with db=db at 1655), 988-1000 / 1025-1052 (swallowed writes), bus.py:88-141 (persist swallowed), bus.py:188 (ordering claim)
findings.finding: The epic path enables fan-out by default; run_manager gathers whole waves concurrently while passing the same AsyncSession to every _dispatch_one_subtask. Concurrent execute/commit on one AsyncSession is unsupported; every affected write site swallows its own exceptions, so the observed failure mode is silent loss of subtask status persistence and event rows (including the per-wave 'subtask.assigned' publishes that fire before slot acquisition), not a crash. The bus docstring's 'Events are ordered per task_id (sequential publish within a task pipeline)' has no enforcing mechanism once a wave has >1 subtask.
findings.evidence: manager.py:2346 + config.py:310-314 (default True; T2-B1 comment); manager.py:1643-1664 (asyncio.gather over wave, single db passed at 1655); swallowing sites: manager.py:995-1000, 1046-1052, bus.py:140-141; ordering claim bus.py:188 with no lock/queue in publish_event (bus.py:181-212). Git commits are correctly serialized by git_commit_lock (manager.py:709-744, 1607) - the DB session is not.
findings.production_impact: Under epic fan-out, subtask status rows and subtask.*/task.blocked events can silently vanish; event-replay consumers (get_unprocessed_events) see gaps; UI subtask progress becomes unreliable exactly when epics run concurrently.
findings.confidence: High on mechanism; Medium on loss frequency (depends on wave size and interleaving)
findings.recommendation: Serialize per-task DB writes under fan-out (per-task asyncio.Lock around publish/status/outcome writes, a session per subtask, or a wave-coordinator queue); update the bus docstring to match the enforced reality.

findings.location: module docstring (ORCH-04-016 claim) vs dispatch_job implementation and real call sites
findings.line: 10-27 (docstring) vs 322-364 (dispatch_job rq branch at 358-359); call sites tasks.py:409, 420, 431, 526, 589, 599, 714, 815, 850, 1113
findings.finding: The module docstring states that every real task-launch call site dispatches via BackgroundTasks.add_task directly and 'QUEUE_BACKEND=rq currently has no effect on real task dispatch'. The code contradicts it: dispatch_job is the single chokepoint all 10 real dispatch sites call, and it branches to queue().enqueue(...) when queue_backend == 'rq'. RQ is wired; the docstring is stale.
findings.evidence: queue_adapter.py:10-27 vs 322-364; grep of dispatch_job call sites in api/tasks.py (10 sites); dispatch_job docstring (329-341) itself describes the real wiring ('Blocker 8 ... the one real chokepoint every task-launch endpoint in api/tasks.py now calls').
findings.production_impact: Operators reading module docs will believe QUEUE_BACKEND=rq is inert and may skip queue/worker provisioning or misdiagnose dispatch behavior; classic doc-vs-code contradiction class (cross-flagged to audit 11).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the docstring to describe the current dispatch_job behavior for both backends (and remove the ORCH-04-016 'not wired' claim or restate it as historical).

findings.location: pipeline_approve vs _dispatch_decision plan_review - dual approval endpoints with inconsistent gating
findings.line: tasks.py:762-824 (stage check only, no CAS/row consumption); approvals.py:83-145 (CAS row flip, no stage check); agents.py:283-375 (resume; final transition CAS at 345)
findings.finding: Two endpoints can initiate the same plan resume. pipeline_approve gates only on pipeline_state.stage == 'awaiting_approval' and consumes no pending-approval row; the approvals path CAS-flips the row but does not check pipeline_state. Neither invalidates the other: two rapid approvals (or one via each endpoint) both dispatch resume_planning_pipeline; the double graph resume and a stale 'pending' inbox row result, while the eventual double launch_manager spawn is prevented by the final atomic transition_task CAS (loser takes TransitionError into the log-only handler).
findings.evidence: tasks.py:793-798 (stage check), 815-823 (dispatch); approvals.py:83-145 (plan_review path), approval_gate.py:183-231 (CAS); agents.py:343-352 (transition then spawn), 372-375 (generic handler swallows TransitionError); repository.py:377-435 (CAS).
findings.production_impact: Double-click approval noise: redundant graph resumes, log-only failure lines, and an approval inbox item that can remain pending after the plan was approved elsewhere. Bounded - no double coding run.
findings.confidence: Medium (mechanism verified; real-world duplicate rate unproven)
findings.recommendation: Single authority: have pipeline_approve also CAS-flip (or delete) the pending row, or have the approvals path require the pipeline stage; document which endpoint the UI uses.

findings.location: _launch_epic_manager exception handler - epic stranded in non-terminal status
findings.finding: A hard exception escaping the epic graph is only logged. The epic remains in whatever status the last node set (pending/planning/coding) with halt_reason unset, and no endpoint can recover it: batch-review lists only ready_for_review/pending_cost_approval; approve/reject require those plus halted; approve-cost requires pending_cost_approval. _finalize_node's halted path (which sets status+halt_reason) is never reached on such an exception.
findings.evidence: epics.py:418-419 (log-only); epics.py:186-190, 261, 295, 329-333 (status guards); manager.py:2417-2467 (halted path that would have made it visible).
findings.production_impact: A transient infra failure (DB error in a node) permanently strands an epic invisible to every review/recovery surface; manual DB intervention required.
findings.confidence: Medium (hard exceptions plausible but rarer than the handled halt path)
findings.recommendation: In the handler, reload the epic and set status='halted' + halt_reason (mirroring _finalize_node's halted path) so it surfaces for reject/review.

findings.location: batch_review task filter uses DevTask.status value 'awaiting_approval'
findings.finding: The batch-review task query filters DevTask.status.in_(['ready_for_review', 'awaiting_approval']), but 'awaiting_approval' is not in VALID_TRANSITIONS and no writer sets DevTask.status to it (the string only exists as pipeline_state.stage). Plan-awaiting tasks are in status 'planning', so the filter's stated intent (docstring L183) is not implemented and the value is dead.
findings.evidence: epics.py:195; db/models.py:30-99 (VALID_TRANSITIONS has no 'awaiting_approval' key or target); grep for 'awaiting_approval' shows only pipeline_state usage (agents.py:184, tasks.py:794) and this filter; run_task transitions tasks to 'planning' (tasks.py:399, 512).
findings.production_impact: The batch-review surface cannot list plan-awaiting tasks (only the approvals inbox reaches them); an operator relying on batch-review sees an incomplete queue.
findings.recommendation: Either join pipeline_state and filter stage=='awaiting_approval' with task status 'planning', or drop the dead value and correct the docstring.
